explain.say: Muscles and bones are tied together by tough cables made mostly of a protein called collagen. There are two kinds: tendons and ligaments.

explain.say: Tendons join muscles to bones. When a muscle contracts, its tendon passes the pull on to the bone, a bit like a rope from a winch. The Achilles tendon joins your calf muscle to your heel.

explain.say: Ligaments join bone to bone across a joint. They are like strong straps that hold the joint together and stop it bending the wrong way, such as the ligaments inside your knee.

faq.q: What is the difference between a tendon and a ligament?
faq.a: A tendon joins a muscle to a bone and transmits the muscle's pull. A ligament joins one bone to another at a joint and holds the joint stable. Both are made mostly of collagen.
Ligaments are tough bands that connect bones at joints. They keep the joint together and limit movement in directions it should not go.
asks: Tell me about the knee ligaments

faq.q: What does the Achilles tendon do?
faq.a: The Achilles tendon joins the calf muscles to the heel bone. When the calf muscles contract they pull the heel up, letting you rise on your toes, walk, run and jump. It is the thickest, strongest tendon in the body.
asks: Tell me about the Achilles tendon

faq.a: Mostly collagen, a strong rope-like protein, arranged in long parallel fibres. That makes tendons very strong when pulled, but not very stretchy.

faq.q: Why do tendons and ligaments heal slowly?
faq.a: They have a much smaller blood supply than muscle, so fewer cells and nutrients reach them, and repair takes longer.

facts: The Achilles tendon is the thickest and strongest tendon in the human body.
Tendons and ligaments are made mainly of type I collagen.

quiz.why: Ligaments connect bones to each other at joints.
